- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.4), model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward slightly to avoid excessive sell-off bias.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., > +1.5% from prior peak), model often overshoots; reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% to account for mean reversion.  
- If sentiment is mixed or neutral (e.g., ±0.2), model frequently underestimates volatility; add 0.3–0.7% buffer to forecast to capture noise.  
- Forecasts with high lag (e.g., 10+ days behind recent trend) show persistent underestimation; align with 3–5 day moving average of recent history.  
- When sentiment turns positive after a downtrend, model often fails to capture momentum; increase forecast slope by 0.1–0.3% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
